outputs.L1: A method for dispatching buildings during a demand response program event includes generating data sets for each building, each data set comprising energy consumption values and corresponding time and outside temperature values. The energy consumption values within each data set are shifted, relative to the corresponding time and outside temperature values, by one of a plurality of lag values, each lag value being different from the others. The method further includes performing a nonlinear parabolic analysis on each data set to yield machine learning model parameters and a residual; determining, from all yielded residuals, a least-valued residual, the least-valued residual indicating a corresponding energy lag for each building; and using the energy lags for all buildings to generate a dispatch schedule for the demand response program event according to a prioritization of the energy lags.
outputs.L2: A technique for scheduling buildings during a demand response event involves creating separate data sets for each building. Each data set includes energy usage measurements matched with associated time and outdoor temperature information, with the energy usage data offset relative to the time and temperature data by a selected lag value. The lag value used for each set is chosen from multiple possible lag values, each of which differs from the others. A non-linear parabolic evaluation is then applied to every data set to produce machine-learning model parameters and a residual value. Among the resulting residuals, the smallest residual is identified, and that minimum residual represents the energy lag associated with the respective building. The energy lags determined for all buildings are then used to create a dispatch plan for the demand response event, with the buildings prioritized according to those energy lag values.
outputs.L3:
The method generates a separate data set for each building. Each data set includes energy consumption values, corresponding time values, and outside temperature values. These data sets provide the information needed to evaluate how each building’s energy use responds to changes in time and outdoor temperature.

For each building, the energy consumption values are shifted relative to the time and temperature values using a range of different lag values. Each lag represents a possible delay between changes in external conditions or operating schedules and the resulting change in the building’s energy consumption. By applying multiple lag values, the method can test which delay best represents the actual energy behavior of the building.

A non-linear parabolic analysis is then performed on each lag-adjusted data set. This analysis produces machine learning model parameters that describe the relationship between energy consumption, time, and outside temperature. The analysis also produces residual values, which indicate the difference between the model’s predicted energy consumption and the actual measured energy consumption for each tested lag.

The residuals are compared for each building. The lag value associated with the lowest residual is identified as the energy lag for that building. This lowest residual indicates the lag that provides the best fit between the modeled energy consumption and the measured energy consumption data.

After the energy lag has been determined for each building, the collection of energy lags is used to create a prioritized dispatch schedule for a demand response event. Buildings with energy consumption patterns that respond more favorably or predictably may be dispatched earlier, while buildings with longer or less favorable response characteristics may be scheduled later. In this way, the method uses the calculated energy lags to organize and prioritize building participation during the demand response event.
outputs.L4:
A demand response building-dispatch method is used to determine how quickly individual buildings respond to changes in operating conditions and to organize those buildings for participation in a demand response event. The method begins by collecting historical or real-time energy consumption data for each building, along with associated time information and outdoor air temperature values. Because a building’s energy use may respond to weather and operational changes after a delay, the energy consumption data is transformed into a series of lag-shifted datasets. Each dataset represents a different assumed time delay between an external condition, such as outdoor temperature, and the building’s resulting energy demand.

For each lag-shifted dataset, the method applies a nonlinear parabolic analysis to model the relationship between building energy consumption, time, and outdoor temperature. This analysis estimates model parameters that characterize the building’s demand behavior under the assumed lag. The method also calculates residuals, which represent the difference between the model’s predicted energy consumption and the actual measured energy consumption. By comparing residuals across the different lag values, the method identifies the lag that produces the best model fit. The lag associated with the lowest residual is selected as the building’s estimated energy response lag.

Once the energy lag has been determined for each building, the buildings can be ranked or grouped according to their expected response timing. Buildings with shorter response lags may be dispatched earlier or used when rapid demand reduction is needed, while buildings with longer response lags may be scheduled in advance or assigned to later portions of the event. This prioritization allows the demand response system to create a dispatch schedule that better aligns building responses with grid needs. As a result, the method improves the timing, reliability, and effectiveness of demand response events by accounting for the unique thermal and operational behavior of each building.

After choosing the best solution, action should be taken step by step. A clear plan makes it easier to stay organized and measure progress. If something does not work as expected, adjustments can be made along the way.

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert this invention idea into claim language: for each building, shift energy consumption by several lag values relative to time and outdoor temperature, fit a nonlinear parabolic model, identify the best lag from residuals, then prioritize dispatch based on the lags.
counterfactuals.output:
Below is example patent-style claim language based on the described invention.

---

## Example Claim Set

### Claim 1 — Independent Method Claim

1. A computer-implemented method for prioritizing dispatch of a plurality of buildings in an energy system, the method comprising:

   receiving, for each building of the plurality of buildings, time-series energy consumption data and corresponding outdoor temperature data;

   generating, for each building, a plurality of lagged datasets by shifting the energy consumption data relative to at least one of time and the outdoor temperature data according to a plurality of candidate lag values;

   fitting, for each building and for each candidate lag value, a nonlinear parabolic model relating the shifted energy consumption data to the outdoor temperature data;

   determining, for each candidate lag value, a residual error associated with the nonlinear parabolic model;

   identifying, for each building, a selected lag value based at least in part on the residual errors associated with the plurality of candidate lag values; and

   prioritizing dispatch of the plurality of buildings based at least in part on the selected lag values.

---

### Claim 2 — Residual-Based Lag Selection

2. The method of claim 1, wherein identifying the selected lag value comprises selecting the candidate lag value having a lowest residual error.

---

### Claim 3 — Parabolic Temperature Model

3. The method of claim 1, wherein the nonlinear parabolic model comprises a quadratic model of energy consumption as a function of outdoor temperature.

---

### Claim 4 — Building Thermal Response

4. The method of claim 1, wherein the selected lag value represents a thermal response delay of a corresponding building to changes in outdoor temperature.

---

### Claim 5 — Dispatch Priority Based on Lag Magnitude

5. The method of claim 1, wherein prioritizing dispatch comprises assigning higher dispatch priority to buildings having longer selected lag values.

---

### Claim 6 — Alternative Dispatch Priority

6. The method of claim 1, wherein prioritizing dispatch comprises assigning higher dispatch priority to buildings having shorter selected lag values.

---

### Claim 7 — Demand Response Dispatch

7. The method of claim 1, further comprising transmitting a demand response control signal to at least one building selected according to the prioritization.

---

### Claim 8 — HVAC Dispatch

8. The method of claim 7, wherein the demand response control signal adjusts operation of heating, ventilation, or air-conditioning equipment of the at least one building.

---

### Claim 9 — Lag Values

9. The method of claim 1, wherein the plurality of candidate lag values comprise a plurality of time offsets selected from hourly, sub-hourly, or multi-hourly lag intervals.

---

### Claim 10 — Model Error Metric

10. The method of claim 1, wherein the residual error comprises at least one of a sum of squared residuals, a mean squared error, a root mean squared error, or an absolute error metric.

---

### Claim 11 — Normalization

11. The method of claim 1, further comprising normalizing the energy consumption data prior to fitting the nonlinear parabolic model.

---

### Claim 12 — Filtering

12. The method of claim 1, further comprising filtering the time-series energy consumption data to remove outliers before generating the plurality of lagged datasets.

---

### Claim 13 — Weather Sensitivity

13. The method of claim 1, further comprising determining, from the nonlinear parabolic model, a weather sensitivity parameter for each building, wherein prioritizing dispatch is based on both the selected lag value and the weather sensitivity parameter.

---

### Claim 14 — Fleet Ranking

14. The method of claim 1, wherein prioritizing dispatch comprises ranking the plurality of buildings according to the selected lag values to generate a building dispatch order.

---

### Claim 15 — Automated Dispatch Execution

15. The method of claim 14, further comprising automatically dispatching one or more buildings according to the building dispatch order in response to a grid event, price signal, load-reduction request, or energy optimization objective.

---

## System Claim

16. A system for prioritizing dispatch of buildings in an energy system, the system comprising:

   one or more processors; and

   one or more non-transitory computer-readable media storing instructions that, when executed by the one or more processors, cause the system to:

   receive, for each building of a plurality of buildings, energy consumption data and outdoor temperature data;

   create a plurality of lagged datasets by shifting the energy consumption data relative to time and outdoor temperature according to a plurality of lag values;

   fit a nonlinear parabolic model to each lagged dataset;

   compute residuals for the nonlinear parabolic model corresponding to each lag value;

   select, for each building, a lag value based on the computed residuals; and

   prioritize dispatch of the plurality of buildings based on the selected lag values.

---

## Computer-Readable Medium Claim

17. A non-transitory computer-readable medium storing instructions that, when executed by one or more processors, cause the one or more processors to perform operations comprising:

   receiving time-series energy consumption data and outdoor temperature data for each of a plurality of buildings;

   shifting the energy consumption data for each building by a plurality of candidate lag values relative to the outdoor temperature data;

   fitting a nonlinear parabolic model for each candidate lag value;

   evaluating residuals of the nonlinear parabolic model for each candidate lag value;

   identifying, for each building, a best-fit lag value based on the evaluated residuals; and

   generating a dispatch priority for the plurality of buildings using the best-fit lag values.

---

## Broader Independent Claim Alternative

18. A computer-implemented method comprising:

   determining, for each of a plurality of buildings, a temporal lag between outdoor temperature variation and energy consumption response by fitting a plurality of nonlinear models to lag-shifted building energy datasets; and

   dispatching at least one building based on the determined temporal lags.

---

## Narrower Independent Claim Alternative

19. A computer-implemented method for building demand-response prioritization, comprising:

   obtaining interval meter data and outdoor air temperature data for each building in a building fleet;

   for each building, shifting the interval meter data by each of a plurality of candidate time lags relative to the outdoor air temperature data;

   fitting, for each shifted interval meter dataset, a quadratic regression model of energy consumption versus outdoor air temperature;

   calculating a residual error for each quadratic regression model;

   selecting, for each building, the candidate time lag corresponding to a minimum residual error;

   ranking the buildings according to the selected candidate time lags; and

   issuing demand-response dispatch instructions according to the ranking.
